utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Good morning, everybody. Good morning, to you Madam Registrar. Could you call the case, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. This is case IT-05-88-T, The Prosecutor versus Vujadin Popovic, et al.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you, ma'am. For the record, you would have noticed that Judge Prost is not with us this morning, but she will join us later on for the last session if I'm not wrong. So we are sitting pursuant to Rule 15 Bis for the moment. I also notice the absence of General Miletic. Madam Fauveau is there, an explanation for that, and can we proceed with the sitting?

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, we've requested -- my client asked the detention unit to tell the Trial Chamber that we can proceed without his presence because his family is here. I don't know why this was not done last Friday, but I'm sure that today you will get the -- the accord of my client to proceed without his presence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. In other words, he has confirmed to you that he will be signing a waiver?

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you. For the record, Prosecution, today is Mr. McCloskey and Mr. Thayer. Defence teams, I notice the absence of Mr. Haynes only. All right. I understand that you've got some preliminaries, Mr. Lazarevic? Please, go ahead.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honour. Good morning, everyone. Yes, Your Honour, it's right. We do have one preliminary. It has to do without 65 ter list. We wanted to ask for the Trial Chamber to grant us addition of certain number of documents to our 65 ter list. My colleagues from the Prosecution are already informed. I spoke with Mr. Thayer yesterday, and he basically does not object to the admission of these documents. And just for the record, I would like to read out the number of these documents.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: The admission of or inclusion of these documents?

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: To be included on our list of 65 ter. Yes. Sorry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. I don't think we need necessarily to know the details of these documents. Mr. Thayer, do you confirm what Mr. Lazarevic has just stated?

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. President. Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. So you have permission to include these documents in the 65 ter list. Whether you make use of them or not is your own business. All right. You have a witness this morning? Do you have any other preliminaries, any one of you?

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: No, nothing other than this one.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. So we can start. Mr. Trisic. Could you bring in the witness, please. Later on after the first break, there are two minor decisions that we will give orally relating to some matters raised by the Borovcanin Defence team. Good morning to you, Mr. Trisic.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, and welcome to this Tribunal. You have been summoned as Defence witness by accused Borovcanin. I do not anticipate your testimony to finish today, but we'll try to do our best. Before you start giving evidence, our rules require that you make a solemn declaration to the effect that you will be testifying the truth. The text of this solemn declaration is going to be handed to you now. Please read it out aloud, and that will be your solemn undertaking with us.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you. Please make yourself comfortable.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Who will be examining the witness? Mr. Lazarevic. Please introduce yourself to the witness, and you can then proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: By all means, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Mr. Trisic. Of course, we have already had the opportunity to meet, but for the purposes of the transcript, I will introduce myself. I'm Aleksandar Lazarevic, and I represent Mr. Borovcanin before this Tribunal. Since we speak the same language, I would just like to ask you to wait for me to finish my question before you begin answering your questions so that we do not overlap and so that the interpreters could do their job properly. For the transcript, can you please tell me your first and last name?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC
utterances.text: Dragoslav Trisic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Can you please tell me where and when you were born?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC
utterances.text: I was born on the 5th of January, 1947, in Bratunac.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Can you please tell me where you live now?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC
utterances.text: I'm still living in Bratunac.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Can you please tell us something about your schooling?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC
utterances.text: I was born in Bratunac. I spent my whole career there. I completed elementary school in Bratunac, and after that I completed secondary and high technical school in Tuzla. After that, I completed the higher teacher training college, also in Tuzla.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Very well. Can you please answer one more question, and then we will deal with your work history in more detail. Did you serve your military term of duty in the Yugoslavia People's Army, and if so, when?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC
utterances.text: Yes. I served my military term of duty in the former JNA from 1971 to 1972, and I served in Zadar in the non-commissioned officer's school.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Very well. Can you tell me something about this non-commissioned officer's school? What kind of military term of duty is that exactly?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC
utterances.text: Well, this is a school where conscripts are trained to be reserve officers, non-commissioned officers.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Very well. Can you please tell me now, after you completed your military term of duty and after you completed the non-commissioned officer's school, what did you do then? Where did you get your first job and how your career proceeded after that.

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC
utterances.text: After I served in the JNA, I worked in a school as a teacher. Actually, before I served in the JNA, I worked in school as a teacher. Then after I completed my military term of duty, again, I returned to the school, and I worked there from 1972, late 1972 until summer 1973.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Very well. After summer 1973, what happened with you work-wise then?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC
utterances.text: I was appointed chief of the Territorial Defence staff of the municipality of Bratunac, and I worked there from summer, or rather, July 1973.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Very well. In the meantime, did you have any other jobs?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC
utterances.text: Yes. During a certain period from 1981 to 1984, I was deputy chairman of the executive board of the municipality of Bratunac. I spent three years at this post. After that, I returned to the TO staff.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Can you please tell me what your post was at the TO staff once you came back?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC
utterances.text: Well, this was a little bit different. By establishment instead of the Chief of Staff, I was appointed as the commander of the TO staff.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Very well. At one point did you retire, and if so, when was this?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC
utterances.text: Yes. I retired on the 1st of May, 1991. This was a period when nationalist parties came to power; and in the division of departments within the municipality, since I was not affiliated with any party, I was not suitable for any duties, and I was given the opportunity or it was suggested to me to retire pursuant to the state administration law, according to which after 25 years of work there is the option that a person can retire. At that time, I had 25 years of -- and 3 months of work, and I retired on the 1st of May, 1991.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: All right. I would just like now to ask you about this time you spent as the commander of the TO in Bratunac. At the time, did you have any assistance, and if so, can you please tell us who they were?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC
utterances.text: By establishment, I had four assistants: Assistant for training and operations, the assistant of the commander for organisation and mobilisation, commander -- assistant of the commander for security and intelligence and security, and I also had an assistant for logistics.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: For the transcript to be entirely clear, we are talking about the time before war broke out, so this is a period during the Socialist Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina and the Socialist Federal Republic of Yugoslavia. This is the time that we are talking about?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC
utterances.text: Yes. That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: And can you please tell me now whether at any point you were mobilised in 1992?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC
utterances.text: Yes. I was mobilised in April 1992.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Can you please tell me, who were you mobilised by?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC
utterances.text: I was mobilised by the Ministry of Defence of the Serbian municipality of Bratunac. I received a summons from the ministry to report to the war unit.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Very well. Can you please tell me now, once you received this summons, where were you assigned?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC
utterances.text: I was assigned as Chief of Staff of the Territorial Defence of the municipality of Bratunac.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Very well. At the time, can you tell me who the commander of the TO was in the municipality of Bratunac? By that time, it was already the Serbian municipality of Bratunac?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC
utterances.text: Yes. The commander was Captain Momir Nikolic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Very well. Now, I would like to look at a couple of documents that are important to understand this question. Before I put the questions to you and before you look at the documents, I would like to give you this binder where the documents are chronologically arranged in the order that the questions will be put. This binder has already been shown to my colleagues from the Defence and the Prosecution, so I would like to go through it now.

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: The first document that I would like us to look at is the law on changes and amendments of the Law of National Defence Official Gazette 6/92, and this is document 4D177, and it's marked number 1 in your pile.

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Can you please wait for this to appear on e-court so that everybody could look at this document that we are discussing. Can you look now on the right-hand side. This is the law on changes and amendments. Can you look at Article 1.

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: It states that the words "Territorial Defence and the armed forces" shall be replaced by the words "army." According to your understanding, is this document a step towards the formation of the Army of Republika Srpska and the abolishment of the hitherto units of the Territorial Defence?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC
utterances.text: Yes. Evidently, the organisational and establishment structure was beginning to be changed, and as it states here, the Territorial Defence and the armed forces is being replaced by the Army of Republika Srpska, as it states here.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Very well. The next document is in tab marked number 2 in your binder. That is 4D526 in e-court, and this is a decision on the establishment of the Army of Republika Srpska of Bosnia-Herzegovina, and it bears the same date, the 12th of May, 1992. Do you have that in front of you?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Very well. Can we look at Article 2 of this decision where it says that the units and staffs of the Territorial Defence are being renamed as the command and units of the army whose organisation and establishment will be established by the president of the republic. And since this is a decision of the same date as the previous document, was that a -- one more step towards the establishment of the Army of Republika Srpska and the disappearance of the hitherto units of the TO?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC
utterances.text: Yes. As I said, the TO staffs were being abolished or they were being renamed as the commands of the army units, and the president of the republic would determine how these units of the Army of Republika Srpska would be organised and established. This is what it states in Article 2.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Very well. Can you please tell me if the Bratunac Brigade was formed immediately after the TO units were made part of the system of the army of the republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina, or was there another unit where the TO units from the Bratunac territory were made a part of?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC
utterances.text: No. From the start of the mobilisation, the TO in Bratunac was organised according to the old formation, into the Territorial Defence of the municipality of Bratunac. When this law came out on national defence and this decision on the establishment of the Army of Republika Srpska, and once the organisational and establishment structure of the units was announced, we were part of the 5th Battalion in the composition of the Birac Brigade, which was headquartered at Sekovici.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Very well. Now, once the Birac Brigade was formed or its 5th Battalion, as you said, were you appointed to some post in it?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC
utterances.text: The 5th Battalion of the Birac Brigade was formed in late May 1992. I didn't have any significant function there since the battalion itself was a smaller unit than the existing TO. I carried out the tasks as deputy commander of the battalion who -- and the commander was actually Momir Nikolic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Very well. Can you please tell me whether at any point you performed any intelligence- or security-related tasks?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC
utterances.text: Yes. I did carry out such assignments, but this was in September 1992 when Colonel Sibinic assumed the post of the battalion commander, and I performed these duties for two months in September and October 1992.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Very well, now I would like to look at the next document. This is document in your tab 3, and it's a document 3DP274. The name of the document is the "wartime road or path of the Bratunac Brigade." Let us first look at page 1 of this document.

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: The first page and the first sentence, which is immediately underneath the title "The Formation of the Bratunac Brigade" where it says that the Bratunac Light Infantry Brigade was formed on the 14th of November, 1992. Can you please tell me according to your recollection whether this fact is correct.

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC
utterances.text: Yes, it is correct. The brigade was formed on the 14th of November, 1992.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Very well. And could we please turn to the next page. It is in e-court, page number 2 in English, and could you please look towards the top of the page under bullet point 8. It says: The idea of forming the Drina Corps of -- the Drina Corps was the only establishment unit of the Army of Republika Srpska; and in addition to that, it says: In addition to this unit, there were also Territorial Defence forces organised in five detachments, and so on and so forth. Let me not go through the whole document.

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Tell me, please. These detachments of the Territorial Defence which are mentioned in this bullet point, whose command were they under?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC
utterances.text: They were under the command of -- the command of the 5th Battalion.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Very well. And can we now move to page 6 in the same document, and in English it would be page 8, please.

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Very well. And you will see here that in the upper part of this page -- now, it's good. It says here -- could you please find it. The sentence begins with the following words: "Pursuant to an order of 18 April 1993 from the Main Staff of the VRS." Do you see that part?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: It says here that the TG-1 was formed from the following: Skelani independent battalion, and a few more units are mentioned thereafter. Tell me, please, do you remember that in April 1993 there was indeed a TG-1 that had been formed in the area?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC
utterances.text: Yes, I remember that very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Who was the commander of that tactical group, please?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC
utterances.text: The commander of that tactical group was Colonel Vukota Vukovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Very well. And tell me, please, when we are talking about this tactical group TG-1, who was it subordinated to?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC
utterances.text: TG-1 was subordinated to the command of the Drina Corps.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: And when the units in TG-1 returned, who remained in the area that TG-1 had been in control of?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC
utterances.text: The units of the Bratunac Brigade remained in the area; i.e., it was the 3rd Battalion of the Bratunac Brigade that remained in the area.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much. We will no longer need this document. Thank you. I would like us to move on to July 1995, and I would like to ask you about the structure and composition of the Bratunac Brigade. The 1st Bratunac Light Infantry Brigade, what was its structure in July 1995?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC
utterances.text: The structure of the brigade at the time was as follows: We had a brigade command with staff units and four infantry battalions.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Very well. And now, I would like us to look at the following document, 4D615, and you will find it under tab 4 in your binder. The document is not in e-court, unfortunately, so it cannot be produced, but copies -- I apologise. It seems that the document has already appeared in e-court, so my information is bit outdated, unfortunately. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Did you have an occasion to see this document before?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC
utterances.text: Yes, I did. I saw it as I was being prepared for this trial.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Could you explain the nature of this document, please?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC
utterances.text: This document is -- or rather, represents a list of the names that -- of the people who were in the brigade, the composition of the brigade.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: You mean the brigade command?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC
utterances.text: Yes, the brigade command, and here we can also see --

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: No. That's the next document that we will analyse next.

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC
utterances.text: The brigade command.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: I would like us to dwell upon the structure of the command of the Bratunac Brigade for the time being. We see the commander and the Chief of Staff, and you can see their names?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: And could you please go through the structure of the brigade command as it follows?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC
utterances.text: Of course I can. Why not? In addition to the commander and the Chief of Staff, there was also the operations and training officer who at the time was 2nd Lieutenant Milorad Micic. We had assistant for replenishment and personnel, Dragomir Riskic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: You don't have to give us all the names. We would just like to see the structure of the brigade and the functions that existed.

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC
utterances.text: Yes. There is head of communications. There's an officer for moral, a guidance and religious affairs; there is also the head of intelligence service, or rather, intelligence and security. We also had the assistant commander for logistics. There was also the officer in charge of technical service, the quarter master service officer, traffic service officer, and there was also a treasurer.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: And somewhere around the middle of this document, we can see your name as the assistant commander for logistics?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC
utterances.text: Yes, that's me, Dragoslav Trisic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: And now that you've looked at the entire document, could you please tell me whether it truly reflects the composition of the command of the 1st Bratunac light infantry brigade?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC
utterances.text: Yes. It is a true reflection of the composition of the command of the Bratunac Brigade in the month of July 1995.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And now, let's look at the following document, which is under tab 5 in your binder, and the document number in e-court is 4D569, so I would kindly ask the Court to produce the document in e-court.

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Let us see whether the document has entered the e-court system. It seems that it did. Very well. First, tell us or explain the nature of this document for the Court.

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC
utterances.text: This is a list of the members of three infantry battalions on the strength of the Bratunac Brigade.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Very well. What can you tell us about the document without mentioning any individual names? What was the structure of the battalions? What were they made of?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC
utterances.text: They were made of infantry companies.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Very well. And again, does this document reflect the situation of the battalion as it was in June 1995, or is there anything that you would wish to add when looking at this list?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC
utterances.text: It does not reflect the composition of the battalions in July 1995. During that period of time, we had on the strength of the brigade also a 4th Battalion, the 4th Battalion which was in the sector of Karici and Kravica villages. That battalion had been attached from the composition of the Zvornik Brigade. This means that in July 1995, it was on the strength of the Bratunac Brigade. It was one -- part of the Bratunac Brigade.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: To your best recollection, could you please tell me, when approximately was this 4th Battalion attached to the Bratunac Brigade?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC
utterances.text: I really can't remember exactly when that was. It was there during that period of time, but I'm not sure when it was actually attached to the brigade.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Very well. And now, we will no longer need this document, but I would like to ask you something about the neighbouring units. You said that in the Bratunac Brigade there were four battalions. Could you please tell me who was on your right flank? Which unit was your right-hand side neighbour, to put it that way.

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC
utterances.text: The right-hand side neighbour of the Bratunac Brigade were the units of the Milici Infantry Brigade.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Very well. And when we're talking about the lines of Defence of the Bratunac Brigade and the Milici Brigade, were they physically connected, or was there an interspace between these two brigades where they should have been connected otherwise?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC
utterances.text: The forces of the Milici and the Bratunac Brigade did not have a physical contact or connection. There was an interspace, an empty space between them which was not covered by troops. That space was in the so-called Bokcin Potok.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Very well. Thank you. Could you please tell me, this interspace or empty space that existed between the Bratunac and Milici Brigade, how was it covered? How was it protected from the intrusions from the enclave? How was this empty interspace covered?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC
utterances.text: Yes, I can tell you that. I can explain. That space, that area was mostly mined; i.e., it was a minefield. There were mines in the area. On the other hand, it could have been defended by mortar fire both from the Milici and Bratunac Brigade units; and also in the vicinity, there was also corps artillery. It was deployed in the Rogac sector.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: When we are talking about the corps artillery, could you please be more precise and tell us what corps do you have in mind?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC
utterances.text: It was the Drina Corps.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: What unit are you referring to when you say the artillery of the Drina Corps? What was the name of that unit?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC
utterances.text: Yes, it was the 5th MAP. M-a-p.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much. And let's move on to something else. Tell me, please, in July 1995, were you still in charge of logistics; i.e., were you still the assistant commander of logistics?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC
utterances.text: Yes, that was my duty. I was the assistant commander for logistics of the Bratunac Brigade at the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Could you please tell us in very general terms, what were the duties and tasks of the assistant commander of logistics in the brigade? What were your duties? What tasks did you have to perform in your capacity as the assistant commander for logistics?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC
utterances.text: Yes, I can tell you that. By and large, my duties and tasks were to look at the overall situation in the units to see whether they had enough materiel and technical equipment.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: I apologise. I was not going to interrupt you. Please continue your answer.

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC
utterances.text: This means that when the stock of the situation was taken, we would establish whether there was anything missing, any materiel or technical equipment, and then we would address the superior command and request for the necessary materiel and technical equipment to be replenished, so that unit would be brought up to speed with both materiel and technical equipment.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: When we're talking about materiel and technical equipment, what are you referring to? We are laypersons, so it may mean a lot to us, but in military terms, what would the term imply?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC
utterances.text: That implies the overall equipment starting with weapons, ammunition, clothes, footwear, food, and fuel for motor vehicles.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: And tell me, please, where was the Bratunac Brigade supplied from? Where did all the materiel and technical equipment arrive from?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC
utterances.text: The brigade supplies came via the logistics base of the Drina Corps. That logistics base supplied the Bratunac Brigade with all logistics supplies.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Very well. Were there any other sources from which the Bratunac Brigade received its supplies?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC
utterances.text: Yes. In case the logistics base did not have all the necessary materiel and technical equipment on stock, we were forced to approach the executive authorities of the Bratunac municipality, asking them to provide the missing materiel and technical equipment. Mostly, those were items of food, items of clothing, and footwear, as well as the fuel that we needed for our motor vehicles.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Very well. And just one small clarification: When you were talking about the logistics base, which logistics base were you thinking of? Which unit?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC
utterances.text: That is the logistics base of the Drina Corps.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And let's just continue with a few more questions on the same topic. You as the assistant logistics commander, how did you send out requests either to the Drina Corps or, as you said, to the Bratunac municipality entities? How was that done technically?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC
utterances.text: I would review the state of the supplies for the brigade and establish which items were missing, and then I would calculate the MTS that we were short of for the coming month; and based on that calculation, I would draft a request to the executive board of the Bratunac municipality, which in the meantime was formed by the staff for the supply of the army. And that request of mine would be then submitted to the staff in order to supply the soldiers, the troops, which would specify exactly which of the Bratunac enterprises should provide the MTS that we were requiring according to type. For example, if we were short of fuel, it would be logical that this would be provided for us through the Vihor transport company because they had that in their supplies, and this also applied to the other articles; for example, food. The company would be allocated which would supply specific items.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Well, let us just correct one thing because it seems to me that this is something that was noted down wrongly in the transcript. It's page 18, line 5. Actually lines 4, 5, 6 in your answer. It says here that you would send out request to the executive board of the Bratunac municipality, which in the meantime was formed by the staff for supplying the army. I think there was some sort of switch there. Can you please tell us who formed who? Did the staff form the executive board, or did the executive board formed the staff?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC
utterances.text: Well, it's logical that the executive organ of power formed the army supply staff.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: All right. Very well. I think that this is now clear. Can you please tell me if you recorded what was received and what was spent in terms of the MTS received by the Bratunac Brigade?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC
utterances.text: Yes. A record was kept diligently about all of the MTS received from the economic subjects of the Bratunac municipality.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Can you tell me how you did this?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC
utterances.text: We received the MTS from the companies, and we would draft so-called materiel lists stating precisely the quantities of equipment. And then these material lists were drafted in several copies so that always one copy of the materiel list would be returned to the company that issued the materiel.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Very well. As assistant commander for logistics in the Bratunac Brigade, did you have desk officers who helped you in this work; and if can, so you please tell us who these people were and what exactly their tasks were?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC
utterances.text: Yes. I did have assistants, desk officers, and they were the following people: The desk officer for the technical service in July 1995 was Boza Momcilovic. The -- actually, technical services desk officer -- I apologise. I apologise. I got a bit confused. The technical services clerk was Novak Stojanovic. The medical -- the quarter master service assistant was Boza Momcilovic. The traffic and transport service clerk was the late Pavle Loncarevic. The medical service clerk was Ljubo Bajatovic, and I think that was -- that's it.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Well, there's no need to go into more detail on this. You talked about --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Mr. Lazarevic, what is MTS? What does it stand for? Look at this page --

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: MTS. Materiel and equipment. That's MTS in all these documents.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. Okay. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] My question, Mr. Trisic, was where were the MTS stored that you received at the Bratunac Brigade?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC
utterances.text: The MTS was stored in two facilities, two warehouses as we referred to them. The quarter master materiel, food and clothing, were stored in the former TO warehouse, which we inherited as the Army of Republika Srpska. The other MTS, primarily ammunition and weapons, were stored nearby in the warehouse of the tobacco station nearby.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Can you please tell me where the fuel was stored, the fuel that you received?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC
utterances.text: Smaller quantities, up to 200 litres of fuel was kept there in the warehouse of the brigade in barrels, and if there were larger quantities such as 1, 2, or 3 tonnes, that fuel was stored in the cistern of the Vihor transport company's gas station.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Can you please tell us how, then, this MTS was further distributed once it was received in the warehouse?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC
utterances.text: The MTS was issued upon request of the lower units, i.e., the battalions. The battalions would make their needs known; and then based on what was available, we would distribute the MTS to the battalions.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: My next question is, if the Bratunac Brigade had some kind of transport means, can you remember which ones it had, if it had any?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC
utterances.text: Yes. I remember we had freight trucks, two TAM trucks, two vehicles up to 2 tonnes, which were used as delivery vehicles. One of those TAM trucks, which was up to 5 tonnes, was used to transport equipment. The TAM was requisitioned from the Vihor transport company. We had two military trucks owned by the brigade; these were the TAM-110 and TAM-150, and we also had two requisitioned buses from the Vihor transport company, which we used to transport conscripts.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Very well. I would now like to move to a different topic. First, I would like you to look at tab 6 and the document marked 4D290 in the e-court system. Do you have that document in front of you?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: This is a report of the commander of the Bratunac Brigade to the Drina Corps command of the 16th of June, 1995. Did you have the opportunity to see this document before?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: I don't want to really deal with the gist of the document. What is of interest to me is paragraph 3 of the document where it says: Pursuant to the Drina Corps commander strictly confidential order of the 8th of June, 1995, the 1st Bratunac Brigade has been ordered to form a company. What is of interest to me in this document is that the company is supposed to be located at the school in Bjelovac. That's what it says in the document. Do you see that part of the document, paragraph 3?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Can you please tell us if the school in Bjelovac was used in order to billet military conscripts as it is stated in this document?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC
utterances.text: Yes. It was used to billet these military conscripts.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Very well. Let us now look at the next document. This is document in tab 7, and it's document 4D292. Again, it's a report of the Bratunac Brigade commander to the Drina Corps command dated the 17th of June, I believe.

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Again, in the document, in the first paragraph it says -- it talks about a unit that was in reserve in the Bjelovac sector. Can you please tell me specifically where this unit physically was located in the Bjelovac centre?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC
utterances.text: Also in the Bjelovac elementary school, which was being used for the requirements of the Bratunac Brigade.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Very well. Can we look at the next document. It's tab 8 in your binder, and this is document 4D316.

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: This document is of the 4th of July, 1995. It's sent to the Drina Corps command. The document is an analysis of the combat readiness for the first half of 1995, and we can now look at page 7. Can you find page 7 of the document?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC
utterances.text: I've found it.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: In the English, it's on page 8. In the upper right-hand corner, it says attachment number 1 or annex number 1.

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: And as the document says, this is a review of the implementation of training and participation in courses during the first half of 1995.

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: I would like us to look at the entries in this table, entry under number 1, also 3, 4, and 5, where it says that the place where the training was carried out was the Drinjaca training centre. Can you please tell us what the Drinjaca training centre was?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC
utterances.text: The Drinjaca training centre was a training centre inherited from the former TO. It was part of the Drina Corps facilities. The Drina Corps organised training in this training centre.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Very well. Let's just look at entry 7 here, where it says Bratunac Bjelovar where the training was being carried out. Can you please tell us where this was -- actually was? Where were the participants in the course physically when they went through the training?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC
utterances.text: It was still done in this before -- aforementioned training centre in Bjelovac.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: All right. Let's look at page 10 of this document now. Can you find page 10? In English, it's page 12. I apologise. While we are looking at this, I would just like to make a small intervention for the transcript. You said that this was physically in the school in Bjelovac; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Very well. Did you manage to find page 10? It begins with paragraph 5, "logistics support." Do you have that in front of you?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC
utterances.text: Yes, I've got it.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Can you please look -- I'm going to put the question to you first. Did you take part in the drafting of this combat readiness analysis, and if you did, which section was the one that you worked on?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC
utterances.text: Yes, of course. I took part in the drafting of the logistic support section of this report under paragraph 5.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Well, let's look at this, the last sentence in paragraph 5 where it says, "a staff for army supplies through which the brigade secures all lacking materiel operates at the municipality level." Is this what you were describing in your testimonies, that that municipality organ that carried out these duties?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC
utterances.text: Yes, precisely. That is that organ, the staff for army supplies, and we secured all the MTS that we required through this staff.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: In your best recollection, can you please just tell me who was part of the staff?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC
utterances.text: The staff comprised of the president of the executive board and the directors of companies in the Bratunac municipality area.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Very well. Let's look at the next document in tab 9 in your binder. It's 4D572. And it's a list of military conscripts of the Bratunac Brigade for the month of June 1995. Do you have that in front of you?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: On page 1 -- let's just wait for the B/C/S version of this document to be brought up in e-court. Yes, that's it. And somewhere in the middle of page 1, can you please find the name of Milos Zivanovic, and then in the last column of the title "Unit," it says the military economy. Can you explain the term "military economy."

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC
utterances.text: Yes. The military economy was actually an independent unit which had been established by the Drina Corps. It was, actually, part of the Drina Corps as such, and it served to supply food to the Drina Corps.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Very well. And now on the same page, could you please find the name Janko Zivanovic, whose father's name was Vasilije, and in the last column it says the Bjelovac barracks. Would that be the school that you have already spoken about?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC
utterances.text: Yes, that was the school. Janko Zivanovic was directly responsible for the maintenance of that facility.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Very well. And can we now go to page 4 of this document. Do you see the name of Savo Sijedic [phoen], father's name Nemanja [phoen], and could you please give us the name of the unit under the last column next to his name?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC
utterances.text: It is, again, the Bjelovac barracks, which means it's the same facility as before.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, let's move on to the next exhibit. This is under tab 10, and in e-court it is 4D571. It is a document which is very similar to the one that we've just seen, but it refers to the month of June 1995. On page 1, you will see again -- can you please find the name Janko Zivanovic, father's name Vasilije?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC
utterances.text: Yes, I can. I have.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: And again, we can see that the last column lists Bjelovac next to his name.

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC
utterances.text: Yes, the same school, the same facility.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: The first document that we saw referred to June, and this one refers to July. My question is whether in the month of July this school was still used by the Bratunac Brigade?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC
utterances.text: Yes. It was still used in the month of July by the Bratunac Brigade.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: And now, let's look at another very similar document, which is 4D570, and in your binder it's under tab 11. This is a list of military conscripts for the month of August 1995; and similarly to the previous two documents on page 1, could you please find the name of Janko Zivanovic, and could you please find his unit in the last column. My question to you, whether in August 1995 the school in Bjelovac was also used by the Bratunac Brigade?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC
utterances.text: Yes, it was also used for the Bratunac Brigade in the month of August 1995.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Very well. And now I would like us to move on to a different topic. Could you please find a document under tab 12 which is 4D313.

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC
utterances.text: Yes, I've found it.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Let us just wait for a moment for this exhibit to be produced in e-court. This is a preparatory order by the Drina Corps number 1. The date is the 2nd of July, 1995; and first of all, I would like to ask you whether you have seen this document before.

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC
utterances.text: Yes, I've seen it before. I had an occasion to see it before, and also, while I was being prepared for this testimony I saw it.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: And now let's look at page 1, and let's see who the document was addressed to.

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC
utterances.text: It was sent to all the subordinated units of the corps, to all the brigades.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: In July 1995, was that document received by the Bratunac Brigade?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC
utterances.text: Yes, it was received in July.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Tell me, please, on the receipt of this document, did the brigade command discuss the document?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC
utterances.text: Yes, the command did discuss the document.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Let's look at page 2 in this document at item under (e).

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: It says here, the 1st Bratunac and the 1st military brigade will carry out -- I apologise, will give the troops and military technique to perform combat operations in their respective areas of responsibility. Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Does this speak about the tasks that were given to the Bratunac-Milici [Realtime transcript read in error, "military"] brigade by this order?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC
utterances.text: Yes. This is a very concrete task given to the troops for active combat operations, as it says in here.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Just a small correction in the transcript. It says "military brigade," and it should read "Milici brigade." This is on page 27, line 13. It should read Bratunac and Milici brigade.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Off mic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Let's stay on the second page of this document, and let's look at the bullet point 5.

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: It says here: The corps command shall carry out all preparations for command and control of active combat operations from IKM-1, which shall be put into operation as of 1400 hours on 4 July 1995. According to your best recollection, was the forward command post of the Drina Corps established at the time specified herein?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC
utterances.text: Yes, it was established. The forward command post was established as per this order in the Pribicevac section.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: When you received this preparatory order - and I don't mean you specifically, but the brigade command - was something undertaken in order to implement this order?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC
utterances.text: Yes. We took appropriate measures to establish the unit that was to carry out combat operations and to equip this unit with all the combat gear.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: And you as the assistant commander for logistics in the brigade, what was your task with regard to the implementation of this preparatory order?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC
utterances.text: Our task was to supply the unit with MTS which would be necessary for the unit to carry out active combat operations.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Very well. Let's look at the following document which is under your tab 13. This is P224 in e-court. Could it please be produced.

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC
utterances.text: I have it in handwriting.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Let's wait for the document to appear in e-court. Now that we have the document in front of us, could you please tell me whether you personally wrote this document?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC
utterances.text: Yes, I did. This is my handwriting. I can tell.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: First of all, let's look at the date. The date is the 3rd of July, 1995, and it was sent to the command of the Drina Corps, and the subject is "request for equipment and materiel." It says here: "Pursuant to your preparatory order number 1," and let me not read the whole number, "dated 2nd July, 1995, we hereby request that you urgently provide us with the following equipment and materiel." My question to you, sir, the first with regard to this document is this: Was your document in connection with the one that we just saw under the title "preparatory order"?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC
utterances.text: Yes. It says in the first paragraph that I am referring to the preparatory order number 1, and we are requesting for the command to supply us with the materiel and equipment.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Tell me, please, based on your request, did the Drina Corps indeed supply you with all the things that you requested?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC
utterances.text: Yes, they did, but not in the required quantities but in substantially lower quantities.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Very well. [In English] This would be an appropriate time to take our usual break because I'm going to move to another topic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Certainly. How much longer do you expect your examination-in-chief will last?

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'm pretty confident that it will take the rest of the day.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: The rest of the day. Okay. All right. We'll have a 25-minute break starting from now. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. Mr. Lazarevic, we'll decide the other issues that I spoke to you about earlier on later on in the day so that we do not interrupt the testimony. Go ahead.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Mr. Trisic, now I would like to move on to the following document, which is under your tab 14. The Exhibit number is 4D378. It is in e-court. We'll wait for it to appear.

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: This is an order for active combat operations dated the 2nd of July, 1995. First of all, tell me whether you've had an occasion to see this document before.

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC
utterances.text: I've had an occasion to see the document before.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Let us first look at the last page of this document.

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Can you please scroll down to display the bottom of the document. Can you see the stamp at the very bottom of the document?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Could you please tell us, when was this document received by the Bratunac Brigade?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC
utterances.text: As it says here, it was received on the 5th of July, 1995.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: When the Bratunac Brigade received this document, did the command discuss it?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC
utterances.text: Yes, the command did discuss this document.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: What were the obligations or duties of the brigade command from the moment that they received this document?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC
utterances.text: The duties of the brigade or its obligations were to prepare for the implementation of this order for active combat operations; and based -- or pursuant to this order, we were supposed to draft appropriate documents for our subordinated units.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Very well. Did you work on the copy of the document that we have in front of us?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC
utterances.text: Yes. As you can see, this was our aid when drafting our own documents for our subordinated units.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Very well. Let's now look at page 3 in this document. Could page 3 please be displayed. Somewhere in the middle, you can see that one portion is encircled, and it says here, the Bratunac Light Infantry Brigade with parts of its troops starts an assault. I'm not going to read the entire document, but I would like to ask you whether these are the concrete combat tasks that the Bratunac Brigade received with regard to the order.

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC
utterances.text: Yes. These are very concrete combat tasks for the brigade itself.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Let's now go back to the last page of this document once again.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Thayer.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. I note that the e-court version because of some highlighting has a particular line blacked out. It's illegible. I have the original of the document which -- in which you can read the top line which is illegible as it stands on e-court. I don't know if my friend wishes to use it, but I have the original here. It's certainly more legible than what we've placed in e-court.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Is the first line important for --

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: This is very useful. I don't find it particularly important, but if need be, I mean, it's very useful to know that we have the original of the document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. We'll do just that. We'll put it on the ELMO, please. Thank you, Mr. Thayer. The ERN number, last three digits is 381.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Correct, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Now, on this page under number 6, it says under 9, "logistic support," and in further text we can follow all the way up to item 11. Would this part of the order refer to the logistics support, i.e., to yourself as the assistant commander for logistics support in the Bratunac Brigade?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC
utterances.text: Yes. It refers to the part of the task that was to be carried out by the logistics support of the brigade.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Very well. And did you enter something on this copy, or did you do something with regard to this copy?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC
utterances.text: Yes. As you can see where it says infantry weapons ammunition, in the brackets it says "four units in assault." It's my handwriting. I made these corrections in my own order or for my own order.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: And the other members of the command, did they proceed in the same way as you did, namely, enter some more specific information into the order?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC
utterances.text: Yes. As you can see, the other senior officers made corrections on this order as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: And can you tell us exactly what you were able to notice in the document?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC
utterances.text: Well, from what I can see on page 5, Security Captain Nikolic entered a correction or added the sector for the assembly of prisoners of war should be in the Pribicevac sector as well as war booty.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: And did you recognise Captain Nikolic's handwriting?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC
utterances.text: Yes, I recognised his handwriting. I can see that it's characteristic. As far as some letters are concerned, I recognise it. And also, we worked together before the war.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. In order to clarify this a little bit more, I don't need to use this document anymore. I would like to look at what is in tab 15 in your binder, and that is 4D605, pages 6 and 7 of this document.

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Do you have that in front of you?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Well, let's look -- let's wait until this appears in the e-court.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: The document that we need has ERN number -- oh, yes, that's the one.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Were you able to notice the handwriting on this document as well?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes. It's evidently a document written by Captain Nikolic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Very well. The next document that I wanted to look at is number 16 in your bundle, and it is document --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the counsel please repeat the number of the document.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm going to wait for it to appear in e-court. Let me just repeat the number of the document. It's P3025.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Very well. This is a document of the 1st Light Infantry Brigade Bratunac Brigade of the 5th of July, 1995, and it's an order for active combat actions OP number 3. Let's see who was going to receive this document.

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC
utterances.text: It was sent to the commands of the 1st, 2nd, 3rd and 4th Infantry Battalion, and of course, to the files.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Very well. Let's now look at item 11, which is on the last page in the B/C/S and 6 -- page 6 in the English version, and it refers to logistics support.

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Can you please tell me now, when you had the opportunity to look at the previous document the order for combat actions of the Drina Corps and this document by the Bratunac Brigade, what can you tell us about this document? In what way is it connected to the previous document?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC
utterances.text: Based on the previous document, we -- in order to support combat actions, we approved the cited quantities of ammunition, fuel and -- in order for the assignment to be carried out.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: And are these more precise directives that you talked about that were entered on the order of the Drina Corps?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC
utterances.text: Yes. That is actually making the order itself more specific and more concrete.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Yes. And now I would like to move to the period after the 6th of July, and we know that the VRS forces had entered Srebrenica. Can you please tell us where you were in this period from the 6th to the 11th of July?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC
utterances.text: I was mostly in the brigade command in the logistics company, and that's where I was for the most part, in that area.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Now, I would like to ask you about a person called Bozo Momcilovic. You already mentioned him. What was his function in the Bratunac Brigade at the time before these combat actions started?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC
utterances.text: Bozo Momcilovic was my assistant for the quarter master service.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: I would now like to look at the following document. It's in tab 17 in your binder; and in the e-court system, it's document 4D597.

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Can we just wait a little bit for the document to appear in the e-court system. I know that you already have it in front of you. Very well. This is an order to engage corporal Bozo Momcilovic who had been passed on to the Bratunac Brigade, and the date is the 4th of July, 1995?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Did you have the opportunity to see this document before?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC
utterances.text: Yes, I did have the opportunity to see the document before.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Can you please tell me, who signed the document and in what capacity?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC
utterances.text: The document was signed by Deputy Commander for Logistics Colonel Lazar Acamovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Can you please tell me whether Colonel Acamovic was your superior?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC
utterances.text: Yes. Along the lines of rear supply, he was my superior.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: And can you tell me if this order of the Drina Corps command was executed and whether Mr. Momcilovic was engaged on the forward command post of the Drina Corps as of the 5th of July as it is stated in the order?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC
utterances.text: Yes. Momcilovic, Bozo, was engaged from the 7th [as interpreted] of July at the forward command post of the Drina Corps in the Pribicevac sector.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Just one correction for the transcript. On page 36, line 6, which was the date that you mentioned?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC
utterances.text: From the 5th of July.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Because it says here the 7th of July. So Mr. Bozo Momcilovic's assignment, did that mean that some other tasks were being carried out compared to those that he was already performing in the Bratunac Brigade?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC
utterances.text: Yes. What it meant is that he was appointed as coordinator of logistics support at the forward command post, but he also carried out other tasks, not just the quarter master jobs.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Tell me, from the point in time when he was engaged at the forward command post of the Drina Corps, to whom did Mr. Momcilovic report to from that point on?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC
utterances.text: Momcilovic reported to the assistant commander for logistics, Colonel Lazar Acamovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Now, I would like to put a number of questions to you, and I would like us to look at a certain number of documents that refer to the operation of telephone lines at that time. According to your best recollection, did the telephone traffic function as usual during the Krivaja-95 operation?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC
utterances.text: No. At the time that the operation was being executed, the telephone traffic did not function regularly.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Let us look at the next document. This is a document in your binder in tab 18. This is 4D541.

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Well, we are just going to wait for it to appear in the e-court system. All right. This is a document of the 5th of July, 1995, the Main Staff of the Army of Republika Srpska, the commander of the Main Staff; and the subject of the order is disconnecting PTT communications in the area of combat operations. Can we first look at the recipients of the document.

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC
utterances.text: The document was sent to the commands of the corps and other subordinate units.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Let's look at paragraph 3 of the document briefly, of the order. Can you see where it says: "Exceptionally, if the required procedure..." Can you please tell us what this refers to as issued by the Main Staff commander?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC
utterances.text: What this is about is that the commander in the area of responsibility can more closely decide on the manner that communications would be disconnected or the manner in which they would be used.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: All right. Let's look at the next document. This is document in tab 19 in your binder, and it's document 4D543 in the e-court system.

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: This is an order of the Drina Corps command of the 6th of July, 1995. We can see that it was dispatched to all Drina Corps subordinate units. First, I would like to ask you to look at the stamp that is at the bottom of the page.

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Can you tell me the date that this was received at the Bratunac 1st Brigade?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC
utterances.text: It was on the 6th of July, 1995, that it was received.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Were you informed about the document when it was received at the brigade?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC
utterances.text: Yeah, I probably was.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Very well. Let us now look at the following document. That is document in tab 20 in your binder, and it's document 4D544 in the e-court system.

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Look at this document, please. It's -- let's just wait for the English translation of the document to be put on the screen. All right. We have it now. It's a document from the commander of the 1st Bratunac Light Infantry Brigade to the Drina Corps command referring to the document of the 7th of July, 1995. Can you please tell us how this document is connected to the previous one that we just looked at?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC
utterances.text: We can see from the document that the commander of the Bratunac Brigade is informing the corps command that on the basis of the corps command order, we disconnected telephones in the brigade's area of responsibility for reasons of execution of combat actions in the area of the brigade. It is also stated that command members' telephones and the company director's telephones were not disconnected and they can work only within the local exchange network in the town.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: All right. I think that we have finished with this document. We won't be needing it anymore. Can we now move to the 11th of July, 1995. We have already said that that was the day when the VRS forces entered Srebrenica; and before I put any more questions to you, in reference to this date, I would like to ask you if you know Mr. Ljubomir Borovcanin.

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC
utterances.text: Yes, I do know him.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Can you please tell me when and in which circumstances you made your acquaintance with him.

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Borovcanin came to Bratunac in early 1993. I couldn't really tell you which month it was exactly. He was appointed commander of the police station in Bratunac.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Very well. And please tell me, you know him from that period; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: And can you please tell me, on what terms were you with Mr. Borovcanin at that time?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC
utterances.text: We were on good terms. Our relations were friendly. We would sometimes meet with common friends; we would have coffee and so on.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Do you remember if Mr. Borovcanin at one point left Bratunac?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Borovcanin left Bratunac in 1994 to assume other duties.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Let me ask this: From the moment when Mr. Borovcanin in 1994 left Bratunac up until the event of 1995, did you have occasion to meet him?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC
utterances.text: Yes, I did, from time to time when he came to Bratunac because his parents remained in Bratunac and he used to come to visit them, so I had occasion on a couple of occasions to meet with Mr. Borovcanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: All right. Tell me now, please, on 11th July, on the day when the army entered Srebrenica, did you see Mr. Borovcanin?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC
utterances.text: No, I did not.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Did you have any communication with Mr. Borovcanin without seeing him in person?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC
utterances.text: Yes, I did. I had contact with him from the brigade command.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Could you please describe what type of contact this was with Mr. Borovcanin on 11th July?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC
utterances.text: On the 11th of July in the afternoon hours, I was at the brigade command in the operation centre - this is a large office - and he was speaking with someone. I didn't know at the time who was on the line with him, but at that point the duty officer said, here is Trisic for you, and you can -- you can talk to him. Then I took the receiver; I spoke with Mr. Borovcanin, and we exchanged greetings. I asked him how he was, and he asked me how I was. He told me -- Mr. Borovcanin told me that he was on the way to the corps IKM forward command post and that he was to receive an order from General Krstic and that his unit was on the way and expected to arrive. I told him, because I had previously agreed with Colonel Acamovic, that the police unit that was en route could be accommodated at the building, the school building in Bjelovac. So this was agreed. It was planned for his unit to be billeted in the school in Bjelovac. This is the content of our conversation, and that's where it ended.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: All right. Let us now talk about the 12th of July, 1995. Can you tell us, please, in the early morning hours on the 12th of July, 1995, where were you?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC
utterances.text: I was at the brigade command.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: That morning on the 12th, did you see any senior officers at the brigade command, any senior officers of the Army of Republika Srpska? If so, could you tell us whom?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC
utterances.text: Yes, I did. There were a number of officers from superior command, from the corps command of the Main Staff. There were a number of officers.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Tell us, please, to the best of your recollection, whom did you see?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC
utterances.text: Well, General Mladic was there, the commander, and General Krstic, who was at the time from the Drina Corps. That was mainly whom I saw. There were other officers, but I can't quite tell you who. I couldn't really speculate.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Of course, I cannot insist on this. You are to tell us only what you can remember. Now, on this 12th of July, did you personally attend a meeting with Generals Mladic and Krstic?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC
utterances.text: No, I did not. That was not my level. As assistant commander for logistics, brigade commander, it was not my place to attend a meeting of senior officers.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: All right. Speaking of the 12th, I would like now to show you a document under tab 21. In the e-court system, it is 3D505. Let's just wait for a moment for the document to appear in the English. First let me ask you, it says here Petrovdan, St. Peter's Day, 1995. Tell us, please, did you draft this document?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC
utterances.text: Yes, this is my handwriting.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: This document is entitled "Consumption or Expenditures of Materiel and Equipment," and "we hereby submit the consumption materiel equipment for the period from the 10th to the 12th July, 1995". Tell us, please, what exactly does this mean, the consumption of materiel and equipment for the period from 10 to 12 July 1995?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC
utterances.text: This document indicates that we are informing the corps that the said quantities of materiel and technical equipment was forwarded to the subordinate units. In other words, in this period, the subordinate units were supplied with this materiel, which does not mean necessarily that they had used all that materiel.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: All right. Let us now take a look at the next document under tab 22, Exhibit P110 in the e-court system.

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Let's now first describe this document. This is a document entitled "Providing Buses for Evacuation from Srebrenica Enclave," order from the command of the Drina Corps of 12 July 1995. First of all, let's see who this order was forwarded to, all the recipients.

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC
utterances.text: It was forwarded to all the units and brigades of the Drina Corps.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: All right. Now, let's take a look at the bottom of this document. We can see a stamp there. Can you tell us when this order was received at the Bratunac Brigade?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC
utterances.text: We can see that it was received on the 12th of July at 835 hours.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Can you tell us, please, who was -- who received it, if you can judge by the signature there?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC
utterances.text: It was received by Major Eskic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Can you please just remind us what duties Major Eskic performed in the Bratunac Brigade?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC
utterances.text: Major Eskic was in charge of personnel matters in the Bratunac Brigade.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Tell us, please, did personnel matters include mobilisation?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC
utterances.text: Yes. So to be more precise, he was in charge of personnel and organisation and mobilisation within the brigade.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Did the mobilisation include only personnel or also materiel?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC
utterances.text: Both personnel and materiel.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: And on this day, on the 12th of July, 1995, what duties was Major Eskic performing?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC
utterances.text: Well, based on this, you can see that he was the duty operations officer because he was the one who received this document.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: All right. You've already told us about two buses that had been mobilised from the Vihor company and were used for transport of the troops of the Bratunac Brigade. Tell us, please, on the 12th of July, 1995, were these two buses used for transporting civilians from Potocari?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC
utterances.text: Yes. They were used for that purpose, and you can see from this order that this was ordered and in view of the fact that I was in frequent contact with Colonel --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreter did not hear the colonel's name.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
