utterances.text: [Interpretation] -- this was relayed to me, and these two buses were used for transporting civilians.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: We need the witness to repeat the general's name. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I'm noticing.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could you please repeat the colonel's name that you just mentioned, the name that you just mentioned, the colonel that you were in touch with who ordered for these two buses to be used for transport of civilians from Potocari?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC
utterances.text: Yes. I said that I was in frequent communication with Colonel Acamovic, who was the assistant commander for logistics within the corps; and of course, he relayed this order to me, informed me of it, so it was normal that we would provide these buses for transport of the Muslims from Srebrenica.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: All right. Let me ask you this: In addition to Colonel Acamovic's order, did you receive that -- such an order from anyone else on the 12th [Realtime transcript read in error, "14th"] of July, 1995?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC
utterances.text: Yes. I received an order from Colonel Acamovic to provide large quantities of bread and to supply Potocari with this bread for the Muslim population there.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Could you please just hold a sec. I would like to intervene on the transcript. On page 44, line 24, it says July 14th, and I was referring to July 12. And that's what we were discussing just now, correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Tell us, did you carry out this order of Colonel Acamovic's for the supply of bread and its distribution?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC
utterances.text: Yes. I ordered the logistics sector, the logistics -- the logistics company of the brigade, we ordered them to supply this bread to Potocari and to try to get as much bread as possible in order to provide it for the needs of the Muslim population.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: I apologise. I see that some parts of your answer did not make it into the transcript. Could you please repeat your last answer, especially where it concerns the bakery and your orders regarding that. Could you just repeat what you've just said?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC
utterances.text: Yes, I can. So I received an order from Colonel Acamovic to ensure that there were large supplies of bread that were to be sent to the Potocari sector for the need of the Muslim population. Through the logistics company of the brigade, I ordered that a certain quantity of bread from our own bakery, the brigade bakery, that as large a quantity of bread be provided as possible. In other words, all the bread that was being baked at the bakery at that point, that it should be sent to Potocari and that the bakery should resume with baking more bread.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. I think your answer is now in the transcript as you've stated it. Now, tell us, on this day, on the 12th of July, 1995, did you go to Potocari?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: How did you go there?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC
utterances.text: I went there using -- in my own official car.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Were you alone, or was someone with you?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC
utterances.text: No. I was by myself.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Could you tell us, please, and I don't expect you to tell us the exact hour or minute, but can you tell us approximately when you arrived in Potocari?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC
utterances.text: Well, at midday approximately, around noon.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: How long did you stay in Potocari on the 12th of July?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC
utterances.text: As far as I can remember, I was there for about an hour, an hour and a half.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: When you went to Potocari from Bratunac on this occasion, you drove past the Yellow Bridge, Zuti Most. Tell us, please, was there a Dutch checkpoint, a Dutch battalion checkpoint right when you crossed the Zuti Most?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC
utterances.text: Yes, it was there.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Tell us, please, on your way to Potocari, did you notice whether the Dutch soldiers were still at the checkpoint or not?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC
utterances.text: Yes, they were at the checkpoint, but they did not stop us. We just -- I just drove by without any interference from their part.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Tell us, please, on your way back from Potocari, did you drive by the same checkpoint, and were the Dutch battalion soldiers present there?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC
utterances.text: Yes. They were there on my way back as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: What was the reason for your trip to Potocari on July 12, 1995?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC
utterances.text: The main reason was to check how the order on the supply of bread to the Muslim population and its distribution was being carried out.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: When you arrived in Potocari, what did you see?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC
utterances.text: In the Potocari sector, i.e., in the sector of the transport company from Srebrenica, there was a large number of Muslims gathered there in that sector. Those were mostly women, children, and as far as I can remember and as far as I could see, those were elderly men also. The DutchBat soldiers were separating the Muslim population from the Serb troops. There was a yellow line that they had placed to prevent the Muslim soldiers from approaching -- the Muslim civilian population from approaching the Serb soldiers and vice-versa.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: And did you also have an occasion to see members of the Serb troops; and if you did, what units were those, and what did you see?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC
utterances.text: I did, yes. There were soldiers from various units there, not only from the Drina Corps but from other units as well. First and foremost, there were soldiers from the units of the Bratunac Brigade. Most of them were military policemen, but there were also regular foot soldiers. There were also corps police members there; there were members of the Zvornik Brigade; and there were also individual police officers from Bratunac as well. That would be that, by and large.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Very well. And now, please tell me, on the 12th of July when you were in Potocari, did you see Mr. Borovcanin there as well?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC
utterances.text: No. I did not see him in the Potocari sector on that occasion.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: You've already told us that you saw members of the Bratunac Brigade and members of the military police of the Bratunac Brigade there. Tell me, what could you notice? What were the military police of the Bratunac Brigade doing in Potocari at that time?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC
utterances.text: They were performing their tasks of establishing peace and order in the area. They also participated in the separation of soldiers from the Muslim civilian population.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: When you say "soldiers," you mean members of the Serb forces?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC
utterances.text: Yes, that's exactly what I mean.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Very well, then. Did the military police engage in any activities with regard to traffic, buses, lorries, those vehicles that had arrived in Potocari on that day in order to transport the Muslim population? Could you notice any such thing?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC
utterances.text: Yes. They were tasked with forming the convoy of buses that would be transporting that civilian population.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: I would like us to look at a document which consists of a number of pages, and I will put my question at the end. But first, I would like us to look at some of those pages. This is the log of the duty operations officer of the Bratunac Brigade. This is P220. And first, let us look at page 16 in B/C/S, i.e., page 13 in the English version of the document. I'm going to put my questions to you after we have seen a few entries in the logbook, i.e., several daily reports for certain days; and first of all, I would like to state that based on this report, we can see that the military police were engaged in securing the UNHCR and delivering the Muslim population on Zuti Most to the Serb soldiers in Bratunac. And also, it says that one part of the police forces secured the sick and wounded in the clinic and the passage of trucks transporting refugees from the Srebrenica enclave through Bratunac. And then a reference is made to my duty, but this is not important for our purposes. Let's look at the following page of this same document, the entry first of the 14th and 15th of July.

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: And again, there is a relatively short entry there. It says the police were engaged in escorting Muslim refugees; and then the following page, which also refers to the 15th of July, it says here that the police were engaged in controlling and scouring the area as well as apprehending and bringing in Muslims who had been found hiding in the area. I would like us to look at just one more entry which is relative to the 19th of July on page 21. In your binder, you will see that the ERN number is 00663930. That's the ERN number on the page. This is 3928, so we have to move on two pages further in e-court to get to the page. Yes, this is the page. Do you have the page in front of you, sir?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: It says here, as you may see it yourself?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: "Military conscripts were informing on the ground. There were no other problems. Patrols went to provide security of communal workers in Glogova." Now that we have looked at all of these page, I would like to ask you this: Do you know anything or do you have any information about these entries in the military police logbook? Did you ever have an occasion to see this before? Do you know anything about this at all?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC
utterances.text: In these reports, one can see that the reference is made to the engagement of the military police, mostly when it came to the surrender of the Muslim population, securing transportation of the Muslims, their loading on the buses, and their transfer to Tuzla and Kladanj. That was how things went, and every day it was more or less the same. Muslim refugees were escorted. There was scouring of the terrain, and they call it controlling and combing of the terrain.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Very well, but do you know any details? Are you familiar with any particular details?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC
utterances.text: No, none. Especially about the -- providing security of the communal workers in Glogova. This is a thing that I didn't know anything about. I've just seen it now in the document.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: If you didn't know, you didn't know. It's okay. I'm not going to put any further questions in this regard to you. On the 12th of July, you were in Potocari. Could you please tell me whether you had an occasion to see General Mladic on that occasion?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC
utterances.text: General Mladic was there. There's no doubt about that, and he even addressed the Muslim population gathered there, and he offered them to be transported in the direction of Tuzla, which they accepted wholeheartedly, I would say.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: And let me ask you this with this regard: With regard to the 12th, did you at any point in time enter the crowd of the refugees that were gathered there in Potocari?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC
utterances.text: No, I did not enter the crowd at all.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: This means that you were on the other side of the line, of the yellow line?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC
utterances.text: Yes, on the other side of the yellow line.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Tell me, please, while you were there for an hour or an hour and a half as you've told us, did you have an occasion to see how people were separated, how men were separated from their families in Potocari?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC
utterances.text: No. I did not have an opportunity to see that, to see that detail.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Did you see the arrival of the buses and other means of transportation in Potocari, and did you see that Muslim civilians were being loaded onto those?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC
utterances.text: Yes. I saw the arrival of the vehicles, and I witnessed a moment when Muslims got on the buses, women and children, that is.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: While you were there and when you could observe the Muslim population getting on the buses, did you notice any Serb soldiers or police officers applying any acts of violence against these civilians? Were the civilians beaten, pushed, shoved, or any such thing?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC
utterances.text: No, no. I did not see any such thing. Those were women with young children and elderly. There was no such behaviour on the part of the Serb soldiers towards them.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: On that day, on the 12th of July, 1995, did you have an occasion to see Captain Momir Nikolic in Potocari?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC
utterances.text: Yes, I saw him at the time in Potocari.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Did you talk to him at all on that day? Did you exchange any words?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC
utterances.text: No, I did not have an occasion to talk to him. A lot was going on, and I did not have an opportunity to talk to him.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: What did you see Momir Nikolic doing on that day in Potocari, on the 12th of July, that is?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC
utterances.text: Well, he was there with the large group of soldiers; and as far as I could tell, he was giving tasks to the police officers, what they were supposed to do, what they were supposed to secure, how they were supposed to go about their -- performing the tasks that were ahead of them.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Did Momir Nikolic communicate with members of other units and not only with the members of the military police of the Bratunac Brigade? Did you see that?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes. I saw him in communication with other soldiers. The corps police was there, as well, and I saw this as some sort of coordination in the work of all these units.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Very well. And when you returned from Potocari after that brief stay in Potocari, where did you go next?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC
utterances.text: I went to the brigade command.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Very well. And now tell me, please, where did you spend the rest of that day up to a certain point in time, on the 12th of July, that is?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC
utterances.text: I was mostly in the brigade command. I may have left it for a brief moment, but I was mostly there.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: On the 12th of July, 1995, did you have an occasion to see Mr. Borovcanin?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC
utterances.text: Yes, I did have an occasion to see him.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Could you please describe that encounter, when and where it happened?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC
utterances.text: It the town centre, there was the logistics company. This is where I was billeted, and sometime in the afternoon - and I can't tell you exactly when it was; I must have been with the logistics company in the very centre where Mr. Borovcanin resided and had his apartment - I came across him late in the afternoon. And since we knew each other, we greeted each other. We exchanged a few words. We engaged in a conversation, I would say. And then I learned from Mr. Borovcanin that his unit was summoned to go back urgently to Zvornik to be further engaged in a different task.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Do you know where Mr. Borovcanin resided, and did you reside in his immediate vicinity?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC
utterances.text: Yes. We resided in two neighbouring buildings, and we would very often see each other there. And on that occasion, we also bumped into each other and had a conversation.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: I would just like to make a clear record. It was later in the afternoon or at dusk, rather; is that what you said?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC
utterances.text: Yes, exactly.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: And how long did you spend in that conversation with Mr. Borovcanin?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC
utterances.text: Maybe two or three minutes, five at the most. We hadn't seen each other for a long time, so we exchanged a few words about our common things, things of our common interest.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Very well. And now I would like us to move to a different topic, which is fuel, the fuel that was used for the evacuation of the civilians from Potocari. First of all, could you please look under tab 24 in your binder, the documents 4D613 in e-court.

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC
utterances.text: Yes, I've got it.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Let's just wait for the B/C/S version to be brought up on e-court. Can you please look at the second page because the first one seems to be rather illegible. Yes. Very well, then. Let's look at the document that is in front of us. Tell me, please, whether you already had an occasion to see the document before.

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC
utterances.text: Yes, I saw the document.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: And let's look at the heading. It is a document that the command of the 1st Bratunac Light Infantry Brigade forwarded to the Drina Corps command, and the date is the 2nd of July, 1995, in the document that is in handwriting. However, it arises from the rest of the document that this is for the period between the 1st of July and the 30th of July, 1995. Could you please explain what this is all about.

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC
utterances.text: It is a mistake. The date should be the 3rd -- I apologise, the 2nd of August, 1995, because this is the account of the consumption of fuel for the period starting with the 1st of July and ending with the 31st of July, so this could only be the 2nd of August of 1995, not the 2nd of July.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Very well, and we can see this on the first page in the e-court system. But since the copy is illegible, I decided to show the document that is in handwriting. Can you first, please, tell me if you wrote this document.

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC
utterances.text: No, it wasn't me.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: And do you know who drafted the document?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC
utterances.text: Yes. The document was drafted by my traffic and transportation assistant, the late Pavle Loncarevic, probably that day on the 2nd of August. I wasn't there at the time when the report was supposed to be done, so he did it on my behalf.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Mr. Thayer.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Sorry to be a little slow to my feet, Mr. President. I do have the original of that illegible typewritten document if my friend wishes to show it, but I do have a copy of that, the original.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Well, I'm very grateful to my colleague. I also have a copy. It is hardly legible, but it can be seen that it is dated 2nd of August, 1995. I don't think there is any dispute between the Prosecution and the Defence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay, but can you proceed on the basis of what you have?

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I think so.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. Then let's go ahead.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Trisic, let's look at the document that you have in front of you now. Under paragraph 2, it says "amounts of fuel received in the course of the month." I'm interested in this entry that is evidently the largest quantity of all that was received that month. It's UNHCR D-2, 30.000 litres. Can you tell us what this is about?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC
utterances.text: This is a quantity of 32.000 litres of diesel fuel that we received from the command of the DutchBat. That fuel was received from the DutchBat command and given for the purpose of transporting Muslim population from Bratunac to Tuzla.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Very well. Just so that I would have the information in the transcript, we're talking about 30.000 litres of fuel, and that is paragraph marked 2 in this report?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Very well. Can you now please tell me, these 30.000 litres of fuel, where was the fuel stored?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC
utterances.text: The fuel was stored in the cistern of the Vihor transport company in Bratunac, the 30.000 litres.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Can you please tell me, how was the fuel replenished in the vehicles that actually carried out the transport of the civilians from Potocari?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC
utterances.text: The fuel was directly taken from the cistern and used to fill in the buses that were transporting the Muslim population.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Can you tell me, according to your best recollection, who specifically participated in these activities to fill in the fuel tanks of the buses that participated in the transport?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC
utterances.text: The immediate participants were people from the corps. Colonel Krsmanovic was the clerk of the traffic and transportation service in the corps, and at the time he was in Bratunac.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: And can you please tell me, who did you get this information from?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC
utterances.text: I got the information from my subordinate, the late Pavle Loncarevic, clerk for transportation and traffic, who actually wrote this report.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: And was there any other place where the vehicles were filled with fuel other than this Vihor depot that you talked about?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC
utterances.text: Yes. Since there was a large number of buses and one gas station would not be able to serve all of them, a cistern came from the corps carrying fuel, and it was parked at Vihor's parking-lot located at the entrance to Bratunac from the direction of Milici and Vlasenica, and that is where the fuel for the other number of the buses was used. The buses filled in their fuel tanks from that cistern, the buses that we used in the transportation of the Muslim civilians.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Let's move to the next day, the 13th of July. Can you please tell me where you were on the 13th of July?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC
utterances.text: On the 13th of July, of course, I was at the brigade command.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Can you tell me that day generally, on the 13th of July, did you have the opportunity to see Mr. Borovcanin on that day?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC
utterances.text: No. No, I didn't have the opportunity to see Mr. Borovcanin that day.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: And can you tell me approximately how long you stayed at the brigade command? I'm talking about the 13th.

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC
utterances.text: I didn't stay there for the customary time. Let's say in the early afternoon hours, I was tired because the previous days I was very busy, and because I was tired, I decided to leave early to my apartment to rest.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Was this around 7.00 in the evening, or...

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC
utterances.text: Well, sometime there, maybe even earlier.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Very well. And can you tell me where you spent the night?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC
utterances.text: As usual, I was at my apartment in the centre. I was resting.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: While you were still in Bratunac at the brigade command, did you notice that anything significantly different was happening in Bratunac in relation to the previous day?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC
utterances.text: No, no, nothing particularly important compared to the day before.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Were the transports going on on that day as well?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Well, you already said that you were tired, you went to lie down to sleep. At any point in time, did you find out that on the 13th of July in the evening a large number of Muslim prisoners were brought to Bratunac and they spent that night in the school in buses and in other places in Bratunac?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC
utterances.text: Yes, but I found out about that the next day. I even found out about it from my sons who told me that in the evening, or rather, in the morning. And of course, I found out about it at the brigade command.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: When you found this out, were there still any Muslim prisoners of war in Bratunac, or was that after they had already left on the 14th?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC
utterances.text: Yes, they had already left. The transport had already been completed.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: In the night of the 13th when you were in your apartment, did you perhaps hear any shooting?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC
utterances.text: I can say that I didn't notice anything in particular. Anything that I might have heard was the usual things. Sometimes soldiers fire without any control, so I don't think that I heard anything that was unusual.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Very well. Let me ask you this: Do you have any information about an incident happening at the farmer's cooperative in Kravica on the 13th of July, 1995, when a large number of Muslim prisoners of war lost their lives?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC
utterances.text: Yes, I do have information about this. I heard about it after it happened, of course.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: How much later, approximately, if you can tell me?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC
utterances.text: Well, I can't really tell whether it was that day or the following day, most probably.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: And can you tell me, what did you hear about what had happened there?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC
utterances.text: I heard that military police officer or that a Muslim had attacked a military policeman, grabbed his rifle, and killed him. The other policeman reacted and tried to prevent the Muslims from escaping, who tried to run away after that incident, and then there was shooting and then, of course, naturally there were some dead as a result of that.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Just tell me one more thing about this. Was this all that you heard about that incident? Do you have any other information about that other than what you were told or what you heard from somebody else?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC
utterances.text: No, I don't have any other information. That would be it.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: And can you tell me, you mentioned here a military policeman. Are you sure that he was a military policeman, or...

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC
utterances.text: I'm not sure. When you say policeman, I'm not sure. I'm not sure.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Very well. Let us now move to the next day, the 14th of July. Can you tell me what you did on the 14th of July? Can you tell me something about what your activities were?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC
utterances.text: Well, I'm describing just regular activities, what I did every day, regular activities, regular daily activities.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: On the 14th of July, you as assistant commander for logistics, were you contacted by anybody about the use of resources of the Bratunac Brigade in order to dig any graves?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC
utterances.text: No, nobody engaged me on anything like that.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: And tell me whether if at any point in time you learned that the bodies of those killed in the Kravica farmer's cooperative were buried in a grave in the village of Glogova?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC
utterances.text: Yes. I did have that information a day or two afterwards. I found out from my friend who was engaged on that task that the burial was completed of those who were killed in the Glogova village section.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: You as the assistant for logistics, were you asked to provide vehicles in order to transport the bodies of the dead from the farmer's cooperative to the grave site in Glogova?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC
utterances.text: No. This was not asked of me since we didn't have vehicles in the brigade that would be suitable for such an assignment.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Very well. [In English] If I could ask for a moment to take a break because we are moving to some other topic, and these are documents that are related one to each other.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: No. We need to continue for the next 15 minutes, and then we have the break at 12.30. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: All right. I will proceed then.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Trisic, I would like to move to the next batch of documents that we are going to analyse. First of all, I would like to look at document -- let me just look. That would be tab 25 in your binder, and it's document P239.

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: [No interpretation] First, tell me if you had the opportunity to see this document before?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC
utterances.text: Yes, I have seen it before.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Can you tell me, whose handwriting is it here?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC
utterances.text: This is my handwriting. This is my handwriting.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: And let's establish that this is a daily combat report for the 12th of July, 1995. Can you tell me how this document came about?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC
utterances.text: Yes. That day I came to the brigade command, to the operations room to write a logistics report for the corps. The duty operations officer was Major Eskic, and it was a bit busy, and because of that he asked me to take some paper and to write this report myself. He dictated, I wrote, and the report was then handed over to be delivered to the corps command. And you can see on the page that it was signed by Dragomir Eskic, Major.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: All right. And now let us just look at the first two paragraphs of the document. The first paragraph states: "During the day, the enemy tried to break through or withdraw from the enclave in the Milacevici-Jaglici-Bokcin-Potok direction further on towards Tuzla and Kladanj." And then it says: "Our forces are mopping up the enclave" -- actually, it says here: "Our forces are carrying out an attack on the column..." And then that's erased, and it says: "...are mopping up the enclave and preventing the enemy from breaking through in the above-mentioned direction."

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: And can you please tell us now, what I just read, does this precisely reflect the activities of the Bratunac Brigade on the 12th of July, 1995?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC
utterances.text: Yes. It reflects the activities of the Bratunac Brigade from the 12th of July and on the subsequent days. It was mostly to prevent the breakthrough of the forces from Srebrenica towards Kladanj and Tuzla.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Very well, then. Let's move on to the following document, which is on the tab 26 in your binder. It is 4DP245. Do you have it in front of you? If you do, just let's hold on a little and wait for it to appear in e-court. This is a wrong document. The document that I would like to present is 4DP245.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the counsel please say the number in English.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The English version is all right. I apologise. [In English] 4DP245. [Interpretation] And could we please -- thank you very much. That's it. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: This is, again, a daily combat report by the command of the 1st Bratunac Light Infantry Brigade, and the date is 13th July, 1995. Let's look at bullet points 1 and 2 in this document first. Under 1, it says that the enemy is completely crushed and is trying to escape in groups in the direction of the village of Milacevic and Konjevic Polje. During the search of the wider area of villages of Milacevici and Babuljica, our forces did not meet any resistance. A large enemy group has been successfully encircled in the area of Konjevic-Polje-Kasaba-Pobulce. Under 2, it says that "the main forces of the Bratunac Brigade continue to search the terrain in the ordered direction of Ravni-Buljim-Zvijezda-Siljato brdo." It also says that some of the forces are engaged in crushing enemy forces which have retreated to the aforementioned area. Tell me, please, now that we have seen this daily combat report, does it reflect what on 13 of July were the main activities of the Bratunac Brigade?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC
utterances.text: Yes, this report does reflect the situation and activities of the Bratunac Brigade on the 13th of July.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Very well. Let's look at next document, which is P246, and in your binder it is under tab 27. Again, let's just wait for the English version of the document to appear on the screen.

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: We can see that this document is an interim combat report which was sent by the command of the 1st Bratunac Light Infantry Brigade to the command of the Drina Corps on the 13th of July, 1995. And we can see that a unit consisting of 92 soldiers led by the Chief of Staff was dispatched to the Bracan sector. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: How were the 92 soldiers transported to the Bracan sector?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC
utterances.text: This unit was transported in our buses that we had in the brigade.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Were they the same two buses that we have already spoken about?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC
utterances.text: Yes, precisely so. Those were the two buses because those were the only two buses that we had at our disposal in the brigade.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: And just one more thing I'd like to ask you. On that day, were the buses used for the transport of civilians from Potocari?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC
utterances.text: No, they could not be used for that because we had to have them at a ready to transport this unit to perform the following task.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Very well. I would like us to look at another document. In your binder, it's 28. It is 4D88. I believe we have the time before the break to analyse this document. Again, this is a regular combat report sent by the command of the 1st Bratunac Brigade sent to the command of the Drina Corps. Let's look at number 1 where it says that "a small part of enemy forces is still surrounded in the area of Bokcin-Potok-Sitjkovici-Mratinci..." And then under 2, it says: "Our forces are searching and clearing the terrain in accordance with order strictly confidential number ..." and I don't want to mention the whole number, and "... part of the forces is participating from our side in the encirclement of enemy forces under item 1." I would like to draw attention to another part of this order where it's a -- of this report where it says that "the Crvna Beretka or the Red Berets platoon was sent at 1000 hours to the area of Milici to join the task in the direction of Zepa." First of all, does this document reflect the activities of the Bratunac Brigade on the 14th of July, 1995?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC
utterances.text: Yes. It does reflect the tasks of the brigade on the 14th of July.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Now, I would like to ask for a clarification, the Red Berets platoon is mentioned here. What was that? What was that platoon in the Bratunac Brigade?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC
utterances.text: That was a platoon, a unit for interventions. We refer to it as an intervention platoon, and we also call it the Red Berets.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Was that part of the Bratunac Brigade?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC
utterances.text: Yes, they were on the strength of the Bratunac Brigade.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. I think we can take the break now. It will be usual 25 minutes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: So the entire bench is present now. We can proceed, Mr. Lazarevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Trisic, first of all, let us go back to some detail from your testimony so far. We looked at the transcript and some of your answers which need some slight clarifications. When you were talking about the presence of the members of the corps military police in Potocari on 12th of July, you meant General Krstic's escorts; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC
utterances.text: Yes. In my mind, that was corps police. I don't know how many of them were there. I could not be the Judge of that.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: And now, a clarification of another answer of yours about Kravica and what you heard. There were some dilemmas here whether those were military police or not. Was somebody who died in the Kravica warehouse, was one of them Krstov Dragecevic [phoen], a member of the special police from Skelani?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC
utterances.text: Yes, I know that. Maybe I did not put it in so many words, but you are right.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Now, I would like to continue where we left off. I'm going to try and bring your testimony to an end, your examination-in-chief, that is. Let's go to 4D595, which is number 29 in your binder. This is a document that was sent from Bratunac from Colonel Ignatovic to the command of the Drina Corps on the 15th of July, 1995. Do you have the document in front of you, sir?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: And now you can see in the part of the document where it says "I've ordered..." bullet point number 4. It says here that the Bratunac Light Infantry Brigade will continue scouring the terrain and the clearing of the battlefield on the axis Bratunac-Konjevic-Polje-Kasaba and so on and so forth. I would like us, also, to look at the part where it says "Proposal," and it says here that the commander of the 1st Bratunac Brigade should be authorised and appointed the commander of all the forces on the ground that were participating in the scouring of the ground and the clearing of the battlefield east of the road, and in brackets it says "and around the road from Kasaba to Drinjaca" because from the command of the Drina Corps there is nobody to be sent for that person. And it says, "Furthermore, if you agree with the proposal under 1, please confirm this by telegram sent to the command of the 1st Bratunac brigade, the first Milici brigade, and to the centre of security centre in Zvornik. "The abbreviation is CSB. Based on this document that we have just seen and that we're looking at, tell me, please, what was the proposal? Who was to be appointed the commander of all the forces that were participating in the scouring of the terrain?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC
utterances.text: In the proposal under 1 it says that the commander of the forces should be Colonel Blagojevic. That was the proposal.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Let's move on to the next document, which is yours, 30, and in e-court this is P254. Do you have it in front of you, sir?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Again, this is a regular combat report sent by the command of the 1st Bratunac Brigade to the command of the Drina Corps, and we can see that it was also sent to the forward command post of the Drina Corps. The date is 15 July. Let's look at items 1 and 2 first. It says here "strong enemy forces in front of P/K." Can you explain the abbreviation P/K?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC
utterances.text: I can't tell you the meaning of this P/K.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: It says that "The 4th infantry battalion on the brigade's right flank are carrying out combat activities and regrouping in the direction of Konjevic Polje and further on." Under 2, it says: "Our forces are still searching the terrain in accordance with your strictly confidential order..." so and so "...dated 13 July 1995, and they are currently on the Lupoglav-Susnjari-Prijanska-Kosa..." and it says here -- yes, Prijanska-Kosa. This is what it says, and so on and so forth. "...Viogor village and Bojna village line, and part of our forces has been sent to the area of the Zvornik Light Infantry Brigade," in brackets, "80 soldiers." And also, a reference is made to sending one part of the forces to the second Romanija motorised brigade, and also, a general mobilisation for compulsory labour has been ordered. Please tell me --

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: If we can split here in transcript on page 67, line 20, my question starts with "it says that the 4th infantry battalion..." So answer and question are not divided.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. Right. We will attend to that later on with the persons responsible for the transcript.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In keeping with this document, what would have been the tasks that the Bratunac Brigade had on that day, on the 15th of July?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC
utterances.text: Well, the forces of the Bratunac Brigade were still engaged in searching the terrain, in keeping with the corps' orders. They were on the line; that is specified in the document, so the tasks were unchanged: Searching the terrain, scouring the terrain, and discovering enemy forces.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Very well. Let's move on to the next document, which is yours, 31, or 4DP255. Do you have the document in front of you?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: In the first part of this document, which is another daily combat report of the command of the 1st Bratunac Light Infantry Brigade dated 16 July 1995, and in the upper part of the document under 2 -- or rather, 1, there's a reference to the sector where the Bratunac Brigade is performing its activities and clearing the terrain. But what I'm interested in is the bottom part of the document. I would like to draw attention to it. It says here: "The commander of the brigade in the course of the day inspected all the units that were blocking the enemy withdrawal..." and in brackets it says, "the Milici brigade, units of the 65th protection motorised regiment, parts of the MUP, and the 5th [Realtime translation read in error, "6th"] Engineering Battalion." And he also defined their tasks and organised their joint action and communications. Just a correction in transcript. It was the 5th engineering battalion rather than the 6th as it is recorded in the transcript. Tell me, please, when you look at this document dated the 16th of July, what was the main task of the commander of the Bratunac Brigade based on this daily combat report?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC
utterances.text: He coordinated the activities of these units in carrying out the remaining tasks of the corps command.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Tell us now, when we think back of the document by Colonel Ignatovic whereby he proposes that the commander of the Bratunac Brigade be appointed as the overall commander for the units engaged in scouring the terrain, can you see a connection between this document and that one?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC
utterances.text: From this document, I can see that they have actually implemented the order of Colonel Ignatovic, and that Colonel Blagojevic is carrying out those tasks.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: All right. Let us look at the next document. That's under tab 32, and in the e-court system it is 4D596 of the 17th -- 16th --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's correction: 16th July 1995.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: -- also sent from the command of the Bratunac Light Infantry Brigade, entitled "Reinforcement With Military Police Units." This document was sent to the Drina Corps command. What I would like you to take a look at is the following part: Colonel Blagojevic is asking or requesting the corps support in sending military police in order to ensure the security of Srebrenica and so on and so forth, but on the second page of this document where it says "brigade units are engaged in searching the terrain, discovering and destroying enemy groups in the area of responsibility of the brigade and beyond," and it also says "part of brigade units are engaged..." and then in brackets it says "(400 men) on four different locations..." and the locations are mentioned as Zepa, Trnovo, Pjenovac, Zvornik, "...the most qualified personnel." Now, tell me. Based on this document, can we see what parts -- where the parts of the Bratunac Brigade, where they were engaged in this area of responsibility?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC
utterances.text: Well, we can see that the most qualified men were engaged in Zepa Trnovo, Pjenovac, and Zvornik areas.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: In addition to these 400 men as stated here, where were the other men of the Bratunac Brigade on the 16th?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC
utterances.text: They were in Bratunac municipality.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: All right. Let's take a look at the next document, tab 33. This is Exhibit --or document 4D5262 in the e-court system. This is a regular combat report of the Bratunac Brigade command for the 18th of July, 1995. Let's just wait a moment for the document to appear in -- on our screens.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Could counsel repeat the exhibit number, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] All right. We have it. Now, let's just take at item 2 of this document. The 3rd and 4th infantry battalions are referred to under item 2. Could you tell us what their assignments were on the 18th of July?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC
utterances.text: They were still engaged in searching the terrain in the area of Pobuda, Hrncici, and Konjevic Polje.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: All right. Let's take a look at the next document right away. This is document under tab 34. This is documents 4DP263. Can you see it in front of you?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: All right. So this is a daily combat report by the 1st Bratunac Light Infantry Brigade for the 19th of July, 1995. Would you please look at paragraph 2 beginning with the words "our units continue to hunt and destroy enemy groups" -- "straggling enemy groups..." And speaking of the 19th, could you tell us the area of deployment of the Bratunac Light Infantry Brigade battalions?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC
utterances.text: From this report for the 19th, we can see that the 1st infantry battalion was engaged in the general area of Zepa, together with the brigade commander. The 2nd infantry brigade was involved in searching the terrain in Gornji Potocari, Bljeceva, and Cizmici and Bacuta; and the third infantry battalion was searched the road between Glogova and Konjevic Polje. The 4th infantry battalion was returned-- or reattached to the first Zvornik Light Infantry Brigade, but we do not know under whose orders. In other words, it was no longer part of the Bratunac Brigade.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: All right. So from this document, we can see the situation in the field in the area of responsibility of the Bratunac Brigade on the 19th of July, 1995; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC
utterances.text: Yes. Let's take a look at the next document. That's under tab 35 in your binder, and it is connected to the previous document, this is document 4DP.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the counsel please repeat the number.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] 4D592. [In English] 4D592.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: While we are waiting for the document to appear on the screens, let us say that this is a document relating to the situation -- or the status of combat readiness in the 1st Bratunac Light Infantry Brigade. The date is 19 July 1995. The document was sent to the brigade commander, and if we take a look at the second page, we can find the author of this document. Perhaps you can tell us?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC
utterances.text: Yes. This is the assistant to the Chief of Staff, Dragoljub Beskic [phoen].

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: If we analyse this document, we can see that the 1st, 2nd, and 3rd infantry battalions are referred to; and the facts or the data that you can see in this document, do they reflect the situation as it was in the field on the 19th of July, 1995, in respect of the use or employment of the infantry battalions of the Bratunac Brigade?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC
utterances.text: Yes. For the most part, it reflects the actual deployment or employment of the battalions of the Bratunac Brigade except for the 4th Battalion, which was at this time not part of the brigade.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: All right. Let's take a look at the next Exhibit that's under number 36. This is document -- or Exhibit P265. While we are waiting for it to appear in our e-court system, to say that this is a regular combat report of the 1st Bratunac Brigade for the 20th of July, 1995, and I would like you to look at paragraph 2 of this document. Can you tell us, it says here that our units continue to destroy enemy forces in the area of Konjevic Polje and Pobuda. Can you tell us whether this, actually, whether this is consistent with the activities of the Bratunac Brigade on the 20th of July, 1995?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC
utterances.text: Yes. This reflects the situation as it was in the field.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much. I have no further questions about this topic. But I would now like to put some questions regarding the last topic that I have, and this is war booty. First of all, I would like us to pull out the document that is under tab 37, and in the e-court, it is 4D598. Can you see the document before you?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: This is an order. In the heading, it says "Republika Srpska Main Staff," and if we look at the last page of this document, we can see that this was the commander of the Main Staff. He was the one who issued this order. The date on the document is 21st July, 1995.

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: This document deals with the establishment of a team to -- which is to be engaged in clearing out the terrain and establishing normal conditions for the population. Under item 2 --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Under item 1, interpreter's correction.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] -- mention is made of who makes up the commission. If you look under 2, you can see under the last item here is the Bratunac Brigade PKP or assistant commander for logistics. Is that you?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Can you tell me, did you ever take part in the work of this commission?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC
utterances.text: No, I did not because I was -- we never met. We never met in this -- we never met as -- with the members of the commission as such.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: All right. Let's look at this document, the next page, 3.7. Can you see, who is made responsible for the implementation of the tasks as mentioned in this document? Could you please tell us who is responsible for the implementation?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC
utterances.text: Well, it says here that it is the commander of the Drina Corps of the Bratunac Brigade, the independent battalion Skelani, the presence of the municipal councils of Bratunac, Skelani, Milici.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: All right. Now, if we look -- all right. Now we can see that everything that you've said is in the transcript. Now, if we look at paragraph 3.8. I wanted to briefly discuss it with you. Could you tell us in keeping with this paragraph 3.8 who was responsible to report to the commander of the Main Staff relating to enabling normal living conditions?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC
utterances.text: Pursuant to this answer, we can see that this was Colonel Lazar Acamovic who was the assistant commander for logistics, and he was to report once a week on the outcome of their efforts and what happened on that far in enabling normal conditions of life in Srebrenica and surrounding places, so the responsible person was Lazar Acamovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: We have -- I have been notified that we have a slight problem with the last answer that you gave regarding paragraph 3.7. Could you please repeat slowly, who was responsible for carrying out this task to the commander of the Main Staff as reflected in this document; but please, take your time so that we ensure that everything in the transcript.

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC
utterances.text: All right. Well, we can see in paragraph 3.7 that the responsible individuals for carrying out this task were the commander of the Drina Corps, the command of the Bratunac Brigade, the commander of the independent battalion in Skelani, and the presidents of the municipal assemblies of Srebrenica, Bratunac, Skelani, and Milici.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: All right. Now, let's take a look at paragraph 9 of this order. Can you tell me when you look at this paragraph what the competencies of the president of this commission, Colonel Acamovic, were, and who was he to address directly if there were any things that needed to be clarified?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC
utterances.text: In item 9, we can see that Colonel Acamovic, the president of this commission, had all the necessary powers to implement the assigned tasks. It is also stated that the Drina Corps command would provide a squad of military police, and for any issues that are unclear, that he may contact directly -- he may contact him directly.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: All right. Can we now look at the last document that I wanted to -- that I wanted you to see and comment on during this examination-in-chief. This is a document under tab 38, and this would be 4D614 in e-court. Let us just wait for it to appear on the screens. Here we have it. Let's just wait for the English version as well. Mr. Trisic, have you already had the opportunity to look at this document?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Can you tell me if you personally drafted this document?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Can you tell me what this document is about? What is the topic of this report?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC
utterances.text: You can see from the document that we informed the corps command about the assembled MTS, the materiel from the former Srebrenica enclave; so from 1 to 9, the materiel and equipment is listed. I also pointed out that the information about the cattle is not available and that this information can be obtained from the military farm that actually got the cattle together.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Just one more thing about this document: Who told you this? Did you have an order to draft this document, or did you do it on your own initiative?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC
utterances.text: It says here that this was required from the corps, and under 18140 from the 23rd of July, the corps required us to provide them with this information, and then the next day we did send this information about the gathered materiel and equipment in Srebrenica.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: All right. Let me just ask you this: The materiel and equipment that is referred to - generator, a cistern, a tent - to whom did this equipment belong?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC
utterances.text: The equipment belonged to the Dutch battalion. We took the equipment along the lines of separation where these equipment and materiel was abandoned by soldiers of the Dutch battalion, except under Article -- item 1, the personnel carrier which was actually directly driven to the brigade command by the soldiers of the Dutch battalion who were leaving the Srebrenica territory, and they surrendered directly to the Bratunac Brigade.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. I thank you, Mr. Trisic. I have no further questions in my examination-in-chief.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Mr. Zivanovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon, Mr. Trisic.

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC
utterances.text: Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: My name is Zoran Zivanovic. In this case, I am defending Vujadin Popovic. Mr. Trisic, you spoke here about a document about the order for active combat of the 2nd of July, 1995. That is 4D378. So I'm now going to ask you to give us some clarifications in relation to that document. Can we look at that document, please. You said that you received this document at the brigade on the 5th of July, 1995, so can you just clarify: At the time when you received the document, was it just this typewritten text without any corrections by hand which you identified later on pages 5 and 6 of this document?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC
utterances.text: Yes. It was just the typed document.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: You saw -- my colleague Mr. Lazarevic showed you pages 5 and 6 of this document, and you saw that there was some corrections made by hand. This is page 5 and in e-court, as well, pages 5 and 6 in e-court. We can stay on page 5. I don't know if you can find it in your tabs; otherwise, just please look at the screen.

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC
utterances.text: It's fine.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Can you please tell me, you identified the handwriting in the upper margin as the handwriting of Captain Momir Nikolic; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: And you were personally there when he wrote that?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC
utterances.text: I recognise the handwriting.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Do you know when he wrote this?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC
utterances.text: Probably on the day when we received the document in question.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Did I understand you correctly, that all of you discussed this document together, the entire command of the Bratunac Brigade, that is?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC
utterances.text: Yes. The commander informed us about this document.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: And at that time, was it then at that time that these corrections were made?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC
utterances.text: Well, we had to do that individually.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Can you please tell me, how does that look when you do it individually? Does everyone have their own copy of the document, or were you all together when you were doing this?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC
utterances.text: No. Usually, we would split the document so everybody would get the part that refers to them.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Does that mean that on page 6 of the same document, these corrections made by hand were made by someone else and not by Momir Nikolic?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC
utterances.text: On page 6?

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, the following page.

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Can you look?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Do you know who did that?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC
utterances.text: I did that.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Did you enter all of these corrections?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Can you identify the corrections that were not made by you?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC
utterances.text: I can. On page 5 at the top, this was done, I believe, like I said, by Momir Nikolic. Then item (e), engineer's support, I can't tell whose handwriting that is, and so on.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Do you know perhaps -- while we are looking at page 2, can you tell or do you know who crossed out some parts of this section on page 5? This is in paragraphs 2 and 3.

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC
utterances.text: Well, it would be logical that this would have been done by Captain Nikolic.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: What about the left and the right margins of the document? Do you recognise his handwriting, perhaps, there with the words "no"?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC
utterances.text: You can see that this was written by the same type of pen, a kind of felt-tipped pen or a marker.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: I wanted to ask you something else now. Can you tell me what the significance was of crossing out the text and entering the written text in the upper -- or the top margin of this document?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC
utterances.text: It was actually adapting the corps's order to our circumstances and to our subordinate units.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: And was that in the nature of a proposal or it already had the nature of an order, what was written by hand in this document?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC
utterances.text: Once this is typed out and is signed by the commander, then it is an order.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: As you can see, it is crossed out here. Can you read the text that has been crossed out? I think it's two sentences.

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC
utterances.text: "The security organs and the military police will determine the assembly sectors and the guard for the prisoners of war and the war booty." Well, there's one more sentence a little bit lower.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. Can you read that?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC
utterances.text: "The security organs will pass on to the subordinate commands and inform them about the application of the security measures in the area of the combat actions."

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Can you tell me, do you know if this text perhaps was included in the order by the Bratunac Brigade commander? I will remind you, this is document 3025. You can look on page 5, paragraph 3 and that --

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC
utterances.text: I'm sorry. Just give me a moment. I have to find it.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Well, perhaps that can also be seen here. Well, I think. Let me see. Let's look at it here on the screen. Paragraph 3 in the English text, that is also on page 5, and it's item 10, the paragraph -- the last but one paragraph.

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC
utterances.text: "The area where the prisoners of war and war booty will assemble is the Pribicevac area, and in the treatment of prisoners of war, adhere at all points to the Geneva Conventions."

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, that is what I meant. Can we look at the last page of that document, although I think that you've already seen it because it was signed by the commander of the then brigade, Blagojevic. What I wanted to ask you, though, is whether we can note that the security organs and the military police were omitted here in this paragraph that you have just read out?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. I would just now like to go back to another thing here. You said that on the 12th of July, you saw Momir Nikolic communicating with the military police officers in Potocari. You remember that answer?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes. I said that.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Tell me, please, were you standing together with them, or did you see them from a distance?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC
utterances.text: Well, as you say, from a distance. I was close by. I wasn't standing with them, but I was standing to the side.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Well, this is what I wanted to say: What was that distance approximately? Can you answer?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC
utterances.text: Well, I don't know. 7, 8, 10 metres.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: And from that distance, 7, 8, 10 metres, were you able to hear what they were talking about amongst themselves?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOSLAV TRISIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Thank you. I have no further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you. Ms. Nikolic, are you going to cross-examine this witness?

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour. I'm going to require 15 minutes to half an hour. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. Let's do the rounds so that we'll know exactly where we stand. Ms. Fauveau?

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation] About 15 minutes, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Mr. Ostojic?

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Same, Your Honour. 20 minutes, about.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Same. Mr. Krgovic?

utterances.speaker: MR. GOSNELL
utterances.text: 20 minutes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. And Mr. Sarapa?

utterances.speaker: MR. SARAPA
utterances.text: 15 minutes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. Okay. So that roughly gives you an idea where you are. Mr. Thayer, I think more or less the major part of -- the main part of tomorrow's first session will be in the hands of the Defence teams, and then you will proceed with yours. Do you still require two hours?

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: I think I will, Mr. President. I'll have to take a look as I go through my material tonight.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Tuesday, the 21st day of October, 2008, at 9.00 a.m.
